narration: There's a tax on being single — and nobody warned you about it. Living alone costs over a million dollars more than being partnered. Here's exactly where it goes.
visual: Dark background. Single person silhouette (circle head, rect body) on left vs. couple silhouettes on right. Dollar signs float upward from the single person. Large $1M+ stat springs in center. Red warning bar: AND NOBODY WARNED YOU. Amber accent theme.

narration: Number one: housing. A couple splits rent two ways — you pay all of it alone. That per-capita gap adds up to four hundred thousand dollars more over thirty years.
visual: Light background. Two house SVGs spring in — amber-roofed house labeled COUPLE on left, red-roofed house labeled SINGLE on right. Per-person cost tags below each house. Animated counter grows to $400K at bottom.

narration: Number two: taxes. Married couples save up to twelve thousand five hundred dollars a year filing jointly. You get zero. Over thirty years, that's three hundred seventy-five thousand dollars gone.
visual: Dark background. Two tax form rectangles — green-header married form with check mark on left, red-header single form with X on right. $12,500/yr saved label vs $0. $375K counter animates at bottom.

narration: Number three: insurance. Auto, health, and home insurers all charge single people more — every single year. The average surcharge hits thirty-four hundred dollars, and they never explain why.
visual: Light background. Car silhouette springs up from below. Two price tags: BASE RATE for couples, +$3,400/YR for singles in red. Three small icons below: auto, health cross, home — labeled by category.

narration: Add housing, taxes, insurance, and other solo premiums together — and the singles penalty hits one million dollars over thirty years. That's a house, paid in extras.
visual: Dark background. Three animated bar chart bars grow upward from a baseline: HOUSING $400K tallest, TAXES $375K, OTHER COSTS $225K. Dollar labels appear above each bar. Total counter animates from $0 to $1M in amber.

narration: You can't opt out of it — but you can build around it. Max your 401k, stack your HSA, invest like the system is working against you. Because statistically, it is.
visual: Light background. Amber piggy bank SVG springs in with coins dropping into the slot. Three checklist items appear with amber accent bars: MAX YOUR 401(K), STACK YOUR HSA, BUILD YOUR OWN NET. Amber follow CTA button at bottom.
